title: Integrated Procurement → Contract → RevRec Accelerator: Approval SLAs, ERP Mapping, and Forecast Sensitivity
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document defines a standardized, accelerated lifecycle for converting procurement requests into signed contracts and recognized revenue events in the ERP/revenue system. It codifies approval SLAs, ERP general ledger (GL) mapping, billing trigger definitions, and forecast sensitivity practices to reduce lead time between customer commitment and accurate revenue recognition. The goal is to: reduce manual handoffs, surface forecast risk earlier, and ensure consistent GL/cutover treatment for dedicated capacity and multi-year subscription contracts.

Scope:

- Applies to: Dedicated capacity reservations, enterprise multi-year subscriptions, and marketplace partner contracts that carry non-standard billable milestones.
- Excludes: ad-hoc usage billing (hosted API pay-as-you-go), internal purchase orders, and one-off professional services SOWs (see separate SOW playbook).

Key definitions:

1) Billing Trigger: The event that creates an invoice (examples: contract effective date, resource provisioning completion, first-production-traffic).
2) RevRec Trigger: The event that satisfies revenue recognition criteria (examples: service available for use, customer acceptance test passed).
3) Cutover Date: The date the contract becomes billable in ERP and appears in forecast.
4) Commitment Type: "Consumption", "Committed Reserved", "Prepaid Subscription", or "Hybrid".

End-to-end process (high-level):

1. Procurement/AE Intake (T-21 days typical)
   - AE or Procurement submits contract intake form in Contracting Portal with: customer tier, commitment type, negotiated commercial terms, required KMS/HSM notes, region/residency, and provisioning SLA.
   - Auto-validation rules check for common missing fields (billing contact, sales order reference, pricing tier).
2. Legal Review + Contract Draft (T-14 days SLA)
   - Legal reserves clause templates by commitment type. For Dedicated reservations include explicit provision/power-on milestones.
3. Finance RevRec Pre-check (T-10 days)
   - Finance runs automated RevRec classification using intake flags. If custom milestone: mark for manual RevRec review.
4. Procurement & Ops Provisioning Coordination (T-7 days)
   - Ops team schedules provisioning workstream; provisioning completion is candidate billing trigger.
5. Signature → ERP Cutover (T+1 day SLA from fully executed contract)
   - Contract metadata pushed to ERP via automated webhook. ERP posts billing event and moves forecast line from pipeline to backlog.

Approval matrix and SLAs (authorities and maximum turnaround):

- AE / Procurement: initial intake and pricing validation — SLA 2 business days.
- Legal: standard templates — SLA 5 business days; negotiated terms — SLA 10 business days.
- Finance RevRec: automated classification — immediate; manual exceptions — SLA 3 business days.
- Ops / Provisioning: schedule acknowledgement — SLA 3 business days; provisioning completion — dependent on resource queue (escalate if >14 days).
- ERP Cutover Owner: Billing Engineering / Finance Ops — push to ERP within 1 business day of signature.

Approval thresholds (example):

- Up to $250k ARR: AE + Procurement approval.
- $250k–$1M ARR: AE + Procurement + Finance.
- > $1M ARR or includes data-residency commitments/KMS: AE + Procurement + Finance + Legal + Head of Sales.

ERP / GL mapping table (reference):

| Contract Type | Billing Trigger | RevRec Policy | ERP GL Code | Forecast Bucket |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Committed Reserved (Dedicated) | Provisioning complete / service available | Recognize over contract term starting provisioning completion | 4001 | Backlog - Reserved |
| Prepaid Subscription (Annual) | Effective date (prepaid invoice) | Revenue deferred and recognized monthly | 4100 | Deferred Revenue |
| Consumption (Usage) | Invoice date (monthly) | Recognize on invoice (point-in-time) | 4200 | Net New Usage |
| Hybrid (Commit + Overage) | Commitment effective date; overage billed monthly | Commit amortized; overage point-in-time | 4001 + 4200 | Reserved + Usage |
Note: GL codes above are illustrative; Finance Ops owns the canonical GL map in the ERP reference.

Forecast sensitivity and scenario guidance:

- Conservative / Base / Upside model: Every large committed reservation should be modeled in three scenarios with multipliers: Conservative = 0.7 * committed value in the next quarter, Base = 1.0, Upside = 1.15.
- Probability assignment: Attach a probability band to each intake based on procurement stage: Intake (30%), Legal Review (60%), Signed (95%). Pipeline commit conversion uses stage multipliers to produce the weighted forecast.
- Sensitivity matrix: Recompute topline variance for changes in provisioning lag. Example: for Dedicated fleet reservations, each additional 7-day provisioning delay reduces recognized revenue in quarter by ~12% (model inputs: average contract term 36 months, evenly distributed recognition).

Automation and webhook contract payload (example):

POST /erp/hooks/contracts  HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <KEY>

Payload (sample JSON):
{
  "contract_id": "C-2027-0456",
  "customer_id": "ACME-231",
  "effective_date": "2027-03-01",
  "billing_trigger": "provisioning_complete",
  "revrec_policy": "amortize_start_on_provision",
  "commitment_type": "committed_reserved",
  "amount_mrr": "15000",
  "term_months": "36",
  "erp_gl_code": "4001",
  "sales_order_ref": "SO-6543",
  "approval_signoffs": ["AE: jdoe", "Finance: apatel", "Legal: mchen"]
}

Exception handling and audit trail:

1. Missing billing contact or GL code at cutover: Billing Engineering tags contract as "awaiting-billing-info" and notifies Procurement; SLA 1 business day to remediate or escalate to Head of Finance.
2. Provisioning missed window (>14 days): Ops opens a provisioning-delay incident ticket; Finance applies forecast crediting rules and adjusts next quarter scenario.
3. Contract amendment with retroactive effective date: Require RevRec manual review and a RevRec adjustment memo recorded in the ERP journal.

Controls and compliance checkpoints:

- All contracts with cross-border data clauses require Legal + Security signoff per Contract Clause Catalog (see related page).
- High-risk clauses (escrow/KMS, special indemnities) trigger a RevRec hold until Legal certifies operational readiness.
- Monthly reconciliations: Finance Ops runs a reconciliation between signed contracts, ERP billing events, and bank deposits; exceptions >$5k escalated to Revenue Controller.

Implementation rollout plan (6 weeks):

Week 0–1: Design and stakeholder alignment
- Review current intake forms and approval flows with Sales Ops, Legal, Finance, and Ops.
- Finalize webhook schema and GL map draft.
Week 2: Automation development
- Build Contracting Portal validations and webhook integration to ERP sandbox.
Week 3: Testing and parallel run
- Simulate 25 representative contract types across commitment buckets; verify GL postings and forecast updates.
Week 4: Training and documentation
- Publish new intake guide, run training sessions for AEs, Procurement reps, and Finance Ops.
Week 5: Pilot go-live (select accounts)
- Monitor SLA adherence and provisioning latency; collect feedback.
Week 6: Full rollout and 30-day review
- Disable manual cutovers for supported contract types and run reconciliation checks weekly for 30 days; report to FP&A.

Appendix A — Example journal entries (monthly amortization for prepaid subscription):

- On invoice (prepaid annual $120k): DR Cash 120,000; CR Deferred Revenue 120,000
- Monthly recognition (1/12): DR Deferred Revenue 10,000; CR Revenue 10,000

Appendix B — Quick checklist for AEs before intake submission:

1. Confirm billing contact and billing email.
2. Select commitment type and attach pricing worksheet.
3. Confirm desired billing trigger (provisioning date vs effective date).
4. Attach KMS/data-residency requirements if applicable.
5. Estimate provisioning lead time and mark expected provisioning completion date.

Appendix C — Frequently asked questions (FAQ):

Q: When should we model revenue in the current quarter if the provisioning completes next quarter?
A: Only include in the current quarter forecast the probability-weighted portion if provisioning has high confidence (>80% and scheduling confirmed). Otherwise, model in backlog for the quarter in which provisioning is expected.

Q: Who signs off on retrospective effective dates?
A: Legal must sign off and Finance RevRec must document the journal impact; the Head of Revenue must approve adjustments >$25k.
